In iplots iset.selected() gives you the cases numbers of currently selected cases.  In Acinonyx the same command gives you a vector of TRUE and FALSE.  With smallish datasets you can use ibar plots of your text variables in both packages to identify selected cases (rotating from the View menu helps in iplots and sorting by highlighted/selected helps in both).

And I know it's not ideal and I have been encouraging Simon to return to Acinonyx, he is just involved in so many interesting projects....

Antony

messages.body_plain:
Simon / Antony / all,

Thanks for the tips, and thanks for chiming in Simon.

I have been able to create a Acimonyx 'application' with commands that
act on iset.selected() using gWidgets.  Nice.

I would additionally like to be able to :

   * install (temporarily) a (modal?) handler for
clicking/drag-recting points which, instead of updating iset.selected,
would invoke a gaction (or something) on the (indices?) of the
selection.  I suppose I could write a loop that watches for changes to
is.selected.  But there must be a better way, I just haven't found it.
 Yet.

 * configure a tool-tip on mouse hover that displays attributes of the
nearest case(s), allowing the attributes displayed to be chosen by the
user (as is done in Mondrian).

I read in a few places about acimonyx's "View menus".  Is this only if
loaded in JGR (which I don't use - living in emacs generally as I do).
 What am I missing?  Should I load it in JGR just to learn something
about acimonyx?

I realize allot of the model is similar to iplots, but, there are many
iplots function that are NOT present in acimonyx, especially those
that interrogate the GUIs state, such as iobj.cur() iobj.get()
iobj.list(), etc. and iplot.cur() iplot.data() iplot.list() etc.  If
there is some document or explanation that you can help me understand
the equivalents in acimonyx I would be happy.

Simon, you write "in iPlots ,,,all variables are implicit".   I think
this discussion argues that you might reconsider this (in a backwards
compatible way, of course).  It has been convenient that acimonyx
displays are magically linked.  However, I think you  need to expose
the magic through the API.   'playwith', which wraps
base/trellis/ggplot graphics, will try to infer the covariates from a
plot call, if there is a data= option.  Perhaps providing a data=
option to iplots, and a link= option allowing explicit linking, and
possibly a heuristic to link two plots if link='on.data' and they have
the same data= or if link=='on.data.length' (the default?) and they
have the same length(data).  Perhaps further the data= could be
inferred as being the environment in which the x parameter resolves
(not sure if that is possible).

Simon, I perfectly well understand if you're off to other great
things.  I certainly benefit from enough of them (parallel/multicore,
RServe, R for Mac OSx comes to mind).  However, I think Acimonyx is
currently uniquely positioned in to allow interactive graphics for
largish datasets driven through R, and may well build on and retain
this position with a few strategic additions, such as perhaps the
above.

If you are interested and find it valuable I will continue to
request/suggest.  If you're on other adventures, I'll be happy to
watch those develop on the nets.

Best,

Malcolm Cook - Stowers Institute for Medical Research - Computation
Biology/Shilatifard Lab

> Yet.

p = iplot(...)
m = marker(p) # the marker is common to all linked plots so you only need to get it once
m$onChange = function(...) # callback when selection changes

Note also that you can use the marker directly via m$selected and m$selected <- ... which may be more intuitive (and also gives you access to the other properties like $values [brushing] and $visible [ghosting]).


> * configure a tool-tip on mouse hover that displays attributes of the
> nearest case(s), allowing the attributes displayed to be chosen by the
> user (as is done in Mondrian).
> 

This can be set explicitly using the $query attribute, but it's not quite working in your case because the scatterplot is cheating and only creating implicit objects. However, what you are describing would be trivially possible by simply adding $onQuery callback to the plot object.


> I read in a few places about acimonyx's "View menus".  Is this only if loaded in JGR (which I don't use - living in emacs generally as I do).

No, JGR has nothing to do with Acinonyx - it was integrated with the old iPlots.


> What am I missing?

Move your mouse to the top of the plot - all menus in Acinonyx are based on cues.


>  Should I load it in JGR just to learn something
> about acimonyx?
> 
> I realize allot of the model is similar to iplots, but, there are many
> iplots function that are NOT present in acimonyx, especially those
> that interrogate the GUIs state, such as iobj.cur() iobj.get()
> iobj.list(), etc. and iplot.cur() iplot.data() iplot.list() etc.  If
> there is some document or explanation that you can help me understand
> the equivalents in acimonyx I would be happy.
> 

In Acinonyx they have been mostly replaced with attributes on the objects (like p$xlim, h$bin.width ...) or generic methods (like primitives(p)). Often the attributes are just a syntax sugar for functions (like $marker for marker(), $visible for visible() etc.).

Some of them are still missing. Partly because I was trying to get the concepts right (that's why marker is now the pivotal place for all linked attributed, for example) - so suggestions are welcome to get the priorities right.


> Simon, you write "in iPlots ,,,all variables are implicit".   I think
> this discussion argues that you might reconsider this (in a backwards
> compatible way, of course).  It has been convenient that acimonyx
> displays are magically linked.  However, I think you  need to expose

> have the same length(data).  Perhaps further the data= could be
> inferred as being the environment in which the x parameter resolves
> (not sure if that is possible).
> 

I agree that having a formula interface and a data parameter is a good idea, and, yes, it was actually planned. However, I would argue that having implicit variables is crucial in R, because you want to plot residuals and other derived variables. But I think you're considering the wrong problem - we already have what you describe already, that's not it - there is a variable registry, a virtual dataset, just as you describe it, but the point is that there is no explicit GUI for it - that's what I was referring to.


> Simon, I perfectly well understand if you're off to other great
> things.  I certainly benefit from enough of them (parallel/multicore,
> RServe, R for Mac OSx comes to mind).  However, I think Acimonyx is
> currently uniquely positioned in to allow interactive graphics for
> largish datasets driven through R, and may well build on and retain
> this position with a few strategic additions, such as perhaps the
> above.
> 

Well, the things I'm off to is RCloud which is roughly Acinonyx + GitHub/Gists + FastRWeb/Shiny + distributed computing, so the idea is to push what we do locally to the web/cloud and this give us much more power (with BigData you seldom find yourself working in the local machine anymore).

But, yes, I apologize that Acinonyx is left sort of undocumented which is the reason why it's not on CRAN yet. And, yes, I am very thankful for feedback -- it gives me much more impetus to continue working on it as it seems that people find it useful.

Thanks,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Jeegar,

On Mar 7, 2013, at 6:51 PM, Jeegar Maru wrote:

> Hi,
>  
> We are using RServe (1.7-0) and the Java client REngine(1.7-0) at OnDeckCapital for one of our projects. It’s been working great so far and we are able to call R scripts from Java. However, we received the following error in Production some days back when creating a file using RConnection. We looked at the RServe code, but it’s doing a lot of byte-level operations and it wasn’t easy for us to figure out what’s causing this error. If someone has any idea about this and how to fix/prevent it, please let us know.
>  
> Stacktrace :
> Caused by: java.io.IOException: Request return code: 70

70 = 0x46 = ERR_IOerror 

This is server-side I/O error, i.e. the server was unable to create the file -- simply fopen(..., "wb") has failed. This is very probably due to permissions on the server - the Rserve instance has to have write-permissions in order to create it and the directory that you are trying to write in has to exist. Are you using relative or absolute path for the file? Make sure you are not creating conflicts between instances -- if you stay in the Rserve working directory you should be fine, but if you go outside, you'll need to be more careful.

If you really want to know more precisely what happens, add perror("") in the if(!cf) statement on line 2494 in Rserv.c -- that should tell you on stderr of the server why precisely it fails -- but as I said, it's probably easier to check that you can write in the location you're specifying.

Cheers,
Simon

> This works.  Great.  But what are the arguments to the onChange
> function.   I can see there are three of them, of class iCallback,
> iObject, and integer.   Can I get back to the plot from them, or
> window, or or?
> 

It's the callback object, the source of the notification and the type of the notification. The most common types defined by the current marker are:
N_TransientMarkerChanged 0x11
N_PermanentMarkerChanged 0x10

The source is the marker -- unfortunately the callback doesn't convert the type so you have to use as.marker() on the argument to get the correct marker class - eventually that should be probably automatic.

Anyway, note that plot or window are not involved here - this is a notification from the marker that the selection has changed - this could happen in many ways that may or may not involve any plots or windows (programmatically, by linking from another marker etc.).


>> Note also that you can use the marker directly via m$selected and m$selected <- ... which may be more intuitive (and also gives you access to the other properties like $values [brushing] and $visible [ghosting]).
> 
> I note that the onChange function gets called when brushing an ihist
> plot.  This seems counter-intuitive since brushing doesnt change the
> iset.selected(), right?  Or does my understanding need fixed?
> 

The marker monitors both transient (highlighting -> $selected) and permanent (brushing -> $value, shadowing -> $visible) marker properties. You can decide to act on one or the other based on the notification type.

messages.subject: Retrieving R error message using Rserve
messages.subject_clean: Retrieving R error message using Rserve
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to extract/return an R error from a parseAndEval call:

REXP myREXP = Rconnection.parseAndEval(myCommand)

For example, I have a some code which uses Rserve to wrap a call to a GBM model.  In case a user sends bad data I would like to be able to capture the R error and return to the user to allow them to attempt to correct their data.  For example:
Error in predict.gbm(myGBMModel, myDataframe, n.trees=1000, type="response") :
   New levels for variable user_type: DUMMY

Running the Rserve daemon in debug mode I am able to see this error in the Rserve log file, but I've not been yet able to successfully return these details back to my calling application.  Is this possible?

I found the following thread online:
http://osdir.com/ml/lang.r.rosuda.devel/2008-05/msg00038.html

However, this approach only provides a little more detail by returning "org.rosuda.REngine.Rserve.RserveException: eval failed, request status: R parser: syntax error" instead of "request status: error code: 127"

Any thoughts on how I can get the actual R message returned?  Thanks in advance.

Anthony
